posts.title: AI Principles — The Parts You Still Own
posts.description: Agents write most of our code now. That’s not a complaint — it’s the best leverage I’ve seen in my career. But it’s created a quiet failure mode: people start treating the agent as the engineer, and themselves as the person who pressed go. The output got faster; the responsibility didn’t move anywhere. posts.title: Agent-First: Designing for MCP and CLI as the Primary Surface
posts.description: Most teams still design software like a human is going to click through it. They build the frontend first, treat the API as plumbing behind it, and bolt a CLI on at the end if anyone asks. That order made sense when the user was always a person. It doesn’t anymore. The fastest-growing user of any non-trivial software product right now is an agent — driving it through an API, an MCP server, or a CL

posts.title: Agentic Engineering — Choosing the Right Level of Guidance
posts.description: Most engineers on our team are using AI agents now. The question isn’t whether to use them — it’s how . And most people get this wrong. There’s a spectrum from full autonomy (“build me this”) to tight step-by-step direction (“use this exact pattern, handle this edge case, call this function”).
